nodes.description: From lymph nodes, virus disseminates via bloodstream to lymphoid organs, liver, and other tissues. Monocytes can be productively infected, potentially mediating systemic spread.

evidence.reference_title: Insights into monkeypox pathophysiology, global prevalence, clinical manifestation and treatments.
evidence.snippet: Once inoculated, the viruses multiply rapidly and spread into the bloodstream to cause viremia, which then affect multiple organs.

Initially, there is a prodrome phase of a few days, which is followed by the appearance of rashes. The dermatological manifestations are in the form of an exanthematous rash, which transforms through a macular, papular, and vesicular phase and disappears after crusting in approximately 3 weeks.
Respiratory manifestations include nasal congestion and shortness of breath that may result in secondary bacterial infections.
Pleomorphic skin lesions appear ranging from macules, papules, vesicles, pustules, some of which may appear umbilicated before crusting over.

evidence.reference_title: Monkeypox Virus Detection in Different Clinical Specimen Types.
evidence.snippet: Our clinical evaluation identified skin lesions as the optimal diagnostic specimen source.

evidence.reference_title: Monkeypox Infection With Primarily Mucosal Involvement.
evidence.snippet: Primarily affecting the sexually active population, these cases present with mucocutaneous lesions mainly localized in perioral, genital, and anal areas.

evidence.reference_title: Triaging cases of fever with vesicular rash relevant to the monkeypox epidemic.
evidence.snippet: Monkeypox (MPX) characteristically presents as a fever with a vesiculopustular rash.

evidence.reference_title: Monkeypox virus: histologic, immunohistochemical and electron-microscopic findings.
evidence.snippet: Initially, it presents with skin eruptions and fevers with diaphoresis and rigors. Clinically, the skin lesions progress from papules to vesiculopustules to resolving eschars.

nodes.description: Orthopoxvirus vaccination with third-generation replication-deficient modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN / JYNNEOS, administered subcutaneously or intradermally in a two-dose series) or second-generation replication-competent vaccinia virus (ACAM2000) elicits cross-neutralizing anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies and T-cell immunity that prevent mpox infection and attenuate disease severity when used as pre-exposure or post-exposure prophylaxis, although cross-protection is incomplete and breakthrough infections can occur years after prior immunization.

evidence.reference_title: Vaccine Effectiveness of JYNNEOS against Mpox Disease in the United States.
evidence.snippet: The findings suggest that JYNNEOS vaccine was effective in preventing mpox disease, and a two-dose series appeared to provide better protection.

evidence.reference_title: Monkeypox in Patient Immunized with ACAM2000 Smallpox Vaccine During 2022 Outbreak.
evidence.snippet: We report a case of monkeypox in the United States in a patient who had been vaccinated with ACAM2000 smallpox vaccine 8 years earlier. Despite his vaccination status, he still contracted disease.

evidence.reference_title: Cross-Neutralizing and Protective Human Antibody Specificities to Poxvirus Infections.
evidence.snippet: Monkeypox (MPXV) and cowpox (CPXV) are emerging agents that cause severe human infections on an intermittent basis, and variola virus (VARV) has potential for use as an agent of bioterror. Vaccinia immune globulin (VIG) has been used therapeutically to treat severe orthopoxvirus infections but is in short supply.
Two vaccines are currently available, JYNNEOSTM (live, replication incompetent vaccinia virus) and ACAM2000® (live, replication competent vaccinia virus)

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of the modified vaccinia Ankara virus vaccine and the replication-competent vaccine ACAM2000 in monkeypox prevention.
evidence.snippet: CONCLUSION: ACAM2000 and JYNNEOS vaccines have proven to be efficient in preventing Mpox even though variations exist in their modes of action and associated significant effects.

evidence.reference_title: Monkeypox virus vaccine evolution and global preparedness for vaccination.
evidence.snippet: It has been observed that smallpox vaccines can be used to protect against MPX. The present article highlights the significant points and various issues for vaccines and vaccinations that should be considered related to MPX.

nodes.description: MPXV enters through skin or mucosa via fusion or endocytic pathways, initially infecting keratinocytes and skin-resident antigen-presenting cells. The virus replicates in cytoplasmic factories (Guarnieri bodies) associated with ER.
